newsitem.title: MEXICO: GE Capital looking at Mexico banking options.
newsitem.headline: GE Capital looking at Mexico banking options.

text.p: GE Capital Mexico, a unit of General Electric Capital Corp, is pursuing the possibilities of buying an intervened bank or a private bank in Mexico, a top official said on Friday.
"We're analysing all the different options...of both government banks and non-intervened banks," Gaston Luken, chairman of GE Capital Mexico, told reporters.
He added that the firm was looking either at an outright acquisition or a joint venture.
He said one of the banks still under consideration was Banco Union, a bank intervened by the authorities in 1994. He said the government was "getting close" to readying the sale.

At a news conference, GE Chairman Jack Welch said there was no firm proposal for any bank, but he said financial areas in which GE Capital planned to be active included the restructuring of the real estate business in Mexico, pension funds, annuities and retail credit.
GE Capital recently sold a $60 million stake in Grupo Financiero Serfin's leasing and factoring unit.
